paper.title: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance
paper.central_claim: WebCoach, a model-agnostic plug-in (WebCondenser + External Memory Store + Coach that retrieves similar past episodes and selectively injects advice via runtime hooks), improves browser-use web agents on WebVoyager across three open-source backbones without retraining, with self-grown (dynamic) memory outperforming externally seeded memory, and lets smaller models approach GPT-4o.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; configured model type only

missing_sections: Coach/Condenser prompts not given (only a worked example)
Figures 2-4 (latency, evaluation queue, bar chart) are not in the text

evidence.quote: WebCoach consistently improves the performance of browser-use agents across three different LLM backbones.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim of consistent improvement over three backbones (Qwen-VL-7B, Qwen-VL-32B, Skywork-38B).

evidence.quote: Notably, smaller base models with WebCoach achieve performance comparable to the same web agent using GPT-4o.
evidence.support_explanation: Comparability to GPT-4o claimed; Table 1 shows GPT-4o 0.653 vs best WebCoach 0.614 (38B) and 0.571 (32B).

evidence.quote: None None GPT-4o 118 10.9 0.653 None None Qwen-VL-7B 144 16.4 0.328 None None Qwen-VL-32B 201 13.3 0.495 None None Skywork-38B 215 10.7 0.473
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines with time, steps and success rate; single run each, 643 tasks.

evidence.quote: External (Frozen) GPT-4o Qwen-VL-7B 333 16.6 0.288 External (Frozen) GPT-4o Qwen-VL-32B 460 10.9 0.547 External (Frozen) GPT-4o Skywork-38B 520 10.7 0.555 External (Frozen) Qwen3-8B Qwen-VL-7B 369 16.4 0.291 External (Frozen) Qwen3-8B Qwen-VL-32B 406 12.2 0.565 External (Frozen) Qwen3-8B Skywork-38B 475 10.3 0.574
evidence.support_explanation: Frozen GPT-4o-trajectory memory with either coach: lowers 7B (0.288/0.291 vs 0.328), raises 32B and 38B by 5-10 points; time up to 2.4x.

evidence.quote: Self (Dynamic) Qwen3-8B Qwen-VL-7B 200 17.4 0.311 Self (Dynamic) Qwen3-8B Qwen-VL-32B 367 11.9 0.571 Self (Dynamic) Qwen3-8B Skywork-38B 395 10.2 0.614
evidence.support_explanation: Dynamic self-grown memory: 7B 0.311 (below 0.328), 32B 0.571, 38B 0.614; single run per cell.

evidence.quote: Dynamic EMS (Qwen3-8B coach): each main agent iteratively updates its own trajectories into the memory store, coached by Qwen3-8B.
evidence.support_explanation: The dynamic store is written by the same agent while it runs the evaluation benchmark, i.e. build stream and eval stream coincide.

evidence.quote: Frozen EMS (GPT-4o coach): memory initialized with GPT-4o trajectories and GPT-4o acting as the coach.
evidence.support_explanation: Seed trajectories come from GPT-4o; whether they were produced on the same WebVoyager tasks is not stated, only same-ID exclusion at retrieval (E008).

evidence.quote: retrieval explicitly excludes any episode whose WebVoyager task ID matches that of the current task, preventing leakage of same-task experience.
evidence.support_explanation: Only same-task-ID leakage is controlled; tasks inside a site are templated and near-duplicates of other tasks are retrievable.

evidence.quote: Only completed episodes that reach a natural stopping point are persisted to memory.
evidence.support_explanation: Admission rule: completed episodes only; both successes and failures are stored with a Condenser-generated success flag; no external validity check.

evidence.quote: The WebCondenser parses these raw traces and condenses them into a structured schema that includes a concise natural language summary, a dense embedding, and key metadata such as whether the task was successfully completed.
evidence.support_explanation: Success/failure label is produced by a small LLM from self-evaluated logs; label accuracy is not validated.

evidence.quote: The Coach is explicitly trained or prompted to remain silent unless it detects high likelihood of failure (e.g., encountering CAPTCHAs, loops, dead ends) or recognizes a better workflow from memory.
evidence.support_explanation: Selective intervention gate implemented by an LLM prompt; no measurement of intervention precision or frequency.

evidence.quote: GPT-4o did not consistently outperform Qwen3-8B as a coach, which led us to decide against DPO-based finetuning of Qwen3.
evidence.support_explanation: Coach is zero-shot in all reported runs even though the intro calls it trainable (E013); a weaker coach matching a stronger one hints that content quality of advice may matter less than generic intervention.

evidence.quote: trainable LLM that decides when and how to intervene mid-episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Text inconsistency: described as trainable in the introduction but used zero-shot in experiments.

evidence.quote: For evaluation, we utilize browser-use agent’s evaluation capability by checking the resulting state of their last action against the initial user query, and determine the success of the task.
evidence.support_explanation: Success is decided by the agent framework's own automatic check; judge model and agreement with human/official WebVoyager evaluation are not reported.

evidence.quote: while the 7B backbone does not benefit, with its success rate slightly decreasing (0.328-0.311).
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge a negative result for 7B, contradicting 'consistently improves across three backbones' in the abstract.

evidence.quote: This explains why the dynamic EMS variant achieves higher success with lower step counts than frozen EMS, despite starting from an empty database.
evidence.support_explanation: Explanation offered without test; confounded by differing seed sources, store sizes, and the build stream being the eval stream.

evidence.quote: When agents iteratively grow their own EMS, they encode decision patterns consistent with their own inductive biases and representation space.
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanistic story about embedding closeness is asserted without an experiment.

evidence.quote: a 14.4-point gain, comparable to the GPT-4o ceiling baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: 0.614 vs 0.653 is a 3.9-point gap, not comparable at this resolution; GPT-4o with WebCoach is not reported.

evidence.quote: yet reduces redundant actions by 1–2 steps per episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 dynamic vs baseline steps: 38B 10.7 to 10.2, 32B 13.3 to 11.9, 7B 16.4 to 17.4; the 1-2 steps claim holds only for 32B.

evidence.quote: Each run covered the full WebVoyager benchmark of 643 online tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Sample size 643 live tasks, one run per configuration; no repeats, intervals or order randomisation reported.

evidence.quote: While average completion time rises due to the additional inference overhead of the Coach and Condenser, the efficiency gain in navigation behavior outweighs the latency cost.
evidence.support_explanation: Reports wall-clock overhead (38B: 215 s to 395-520 s) but not tokens/API dollars or a compute-matched baseline.

evidence.quote: Workflow-oriented stores mine reusable action sequences to improve web and multi-agent performance
evidence.support_explanation: Closest web-memory neighbours (workflow memory) are acknowledged in one sentence; none is run as a baseline.

evidence.quote: However, these ideas have not been fully integrated into mainstream web-navigation pipelines.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated gap is integration into pipelines rather than a measured failure of existing memory methods.

evidence.quote: which retrieves relevant experiences based on similarity and recency, and decides whether to inject task-specific advice into the agent via runtime hooks.
evidence.support_explanation: Recency is claimed, but Section 2.2 ranks by embedding similarity only (E025).

evidence.quote: Once candidate memories are retrieved, they are ranked by their similarity to the current context embedding, which is computed via a normalized dot product between the embedding vectors.
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval is cosine similarity over summary embeddings, top-K (K=5), HNSW-128; no recency term, no utility term, no dedup/forgetting.

evidence.quote: but agents rarely remember mistakes or successes beyond the current task.
evidence.support_explanation: Author problem statement; concrete failure behaviours (revisiting links, login gates, CAPTCHAs) are named but not quantified.

evidence.quote: Notably, dynamic self-experience memory (where agents iteratively expand their own memory store) outperforms externally seeded memories, highlighting that agents learn most effectively from their own trajectories rather than borrowed ones.
evidence.support_explanation: Generalised conclusion from three single-run pairs (38B +4.0 and 32B +0.6 vs Qwen3 coach frozen; 7B +2.0).

signatures.object: External episodic memory store (embedding + LLM summary + metadata per completed trajectory) and a Coach LLM that gates advice injection; actor agent frozen; baseline = browser-use agent with default prompt

signatures.operation: Condense -> store completed episodes only -> at each step retrieve top-K by cosine -> Coach decides intervene/not and writes a one-to-two-sentence advice injected as a system message
signatures.output: Per-step optional advice; grown episodic store
signatures.conditions: Live WebVoyager; 50-step cap; Qwen3-8B or GPT-4o coach, zero-shot
signatures.feedback: Self-assessed trajectory outcome; benchmark auto-judge only for reporting
signatures.selection_rule_data: Completed vs partial routing; same-task-ID exclusion at retrieval; no admission/quality gate
signatures.persistence: FAISS HNSW store; dynamic variant grows over the evaluation run, frozen variant seeded from GPT-4o trajectories
signatures.later_use: Retrieval for subsequent tasks in the same run
signatures.claimed_effect: Success 0.473 to 0.614 (Skywork-38B), 0.495 to 0.571 (Qwen-VL-32B), no gain for 7B

gap.author_gap: Web agents repeat errors (revisit links, stall at login gates, CAPTCHAs) and lack cross-session memory; memory ideas are not integrated into mainstream web pipelines.
gap.checked_gap: Real but thin: repeated loops/dead ends in long browsing tasks are a recognised failure; the stated residual is integration into pipelines, not a demonstrated shortfall of existing web or workflow memories. The non-weight object is a coaching/memory wrapper around a fixed agent.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion-style episodic reflection and workflow memory (Agent Workflow Memory family) -> memory services (Mem0, MemGPT-style layers) -> WebCoach adds a runtime Coach that gates advice and a Condenser to normalise logs. Original neighbour papers are not in the pinned package; only the one-line related-work characterisations are available.
gap.residue: Whether retrieved experience (as opposed to a generic anti-loop nudge) drives the gain; transfer beyond the benchmark; harm to weak actors.
gap.stakes: Wasted steps and failed tasks on live sites; extra latency from coaching.
gap.method_response: Selective LLM coaching grounded in retrieved summaries from past episodes, with a store that grows online.
gap.remaining_gap: No coach-only or memory-only control, no comparison with workflow-memory or other memory baselines, no held-out transfer, weak-model degradation unresolved.
unresolved: Originals of Agent Workflow Memory and similar web-memory methods are not pinned, so the novelty margin over them cannot be verified here.

claims.text: WebCoach improves web-agent success on WebVoyager without retraining
claims.setting: Live WebVoyager, 643 tasks, browser-use agent, 50-step cap; Qwen-VL-7B/32B and Skywork-38B actors; Qwen3-8B or GPT-4o coach
claims.baseline_control: Same agent without memory or coach
claims.selection_vs_test: Memory built from earlier tasks of the same run (dynamic) or GPT-4o trajectories (frozen); same-ID exclusion
claims.counterevidence: 7B declines in all variants; no coach-only or memory-only control
claims.allowed_conclusion: In single runs on this benchmark WebCoach raised success for the 32B and 38B actors and lowered it for the 7B actor; attribution to retrieved experience over generic coaching is not shown.

claims.text: Self-grown dynamic memory outperforms externally seeded memory
claims.setting: Qwen3-8B coach; dynamic vs GPT-4o-seeded frozen EMS
claims.selection_vs_test: Dynamic store built on the eval stream
claims.counterevidence: Gaps of 0.6-4.0 points, single runs, confounded seed source and store size
claims.allowed_conclusion: Dynamic memory scored numerically higher in all three pairs; the explanation is speculation and significance is untested.

claims.text: Smaller models with WebCoach achieve performance comparable to GPT-4o
claims.counterevidence: 3.9-8.2 point deficits; GPT-4o with WebCoach not run
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not supported as stated; they close part of the gap.

claims.text: Gains come from better decisions, not brute-force exploration (steps flat or lower)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Steps are flat or slightly lower for 32B/38B; time increases.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Wrapping 32B/38B open-source browser-use actors with a Condenser+memory+Qwen3-8B Coach improved single-run success on WebVoyager by about 7-14 points at roughly 1.3-1.9x wall time, with a decline for the 7B actor; the contribution of retrieved experience (vs generic coaching) and generalisation beyond the build stream are not established.
unresolved: Held-out or order-randomised evaluation of the retained store
Validity of the automatic success judge and Condenser success labels
Variance across runs on live websites

G.reason: Names concrete web-agent failure behaviours (loops, login gates, CAPTCHAs) and the lack of cross-session memory, but the stated residual is non-integration into pipelines, closest web-memory neighbours are not compared, and the failures are not quantified.

M.reason: Reconstructible plug-in mechanism with a selective-intervention gate that suits the stated failure modes, but no argument or test for why summarised cross-task episodes transfer, no component ablation, and the Coach is described both as trainable and as zero-shot.

X.reason: Three-module pipeline, routing of partial vs completed episodes, K=5, HNSW and hook injection are specified, but prompts, admission gate, label validation, recency (claimed, not implemented), deduplication/forgetting and rollback are absent.

E.measurement.reason: 643 live tasks is a credible benchmark but success is decided by the agent framework's built-in check with unreported judge and no agreement study; the Condenser's success flag is also unvalidated; abstract overstates comparability with GPT-4o.

E.causality.reason: Only four whole-system configurations; no coach-only, memory-only, generic-nudge, random-memory or neighbour-method controls; frozen vs dynamic comparison is confounded; 7B degradation unexplained; weaker coach equalling stronger coach hints advice content is not isolated.

E.holdout.reason: Dynamic memory is built on the evaluation stream and frozen memory is seeded from GPT-4o trajectories; only same-task-ID retrieval is excluded, leaving templated near-duplicate tasks within sites; no train/test split, order randomisation or cross-benchmark test.

E.statistics.reason: Sample size (643) and per-subdomain success counts are given and a negative result (7B) is reported, but single runs on a live nondeterministic web with no intervals, repeats or order variation; some claimed effects are 0.6-4 points.

E.cost.reason: Average time and steps are reported with the overhead of Coach and Condenser acknowledged (38B 215 s to 395-520 s); no token or dollar cost, coach call counts, or compute-matched baseline.

rationale: Memory-coach plug-in helps 32B/38B; single-run whole-system comparisons, stream-built memory, unvalidated judge; consistency/GPT-4o parity overclaimed
